title: Completeness and residue calculation of a completed perfect coefficient model
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subset A$ be a maximal ideal, and put $k=A/I$. On $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/I^n}$, using constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules, zero outside degrees $[a,b]$, and let $M^\bullet=B\otimes_A P^\bullet$ denote termwise extension of the constant complex; perfect complexes are [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Work in the module-sheaf derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $M^\bullet$ is locally derived $IB$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. Its derived residue reduction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] has the canonical isomorphism $M^\bullet\otimes^L_B\underline k\simeq\underline{P^\bullet\otimes_A k}$. For every integer $q$, its cohomology is the constant sheaf of the finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $H^q(P^\bullet\otimes_A k)$, and both $M^\bullet$ and its residue reduction have zero cohomology outside $[a,b]$. The same assertions hold on every covering slice, with the restricted coefficient sheaf. No finiteness of the set $k$, no regularity of $A$, and no perfectness of $A/I^n$ over $A$ is required.

proof.text: Split each finite projective term off A^r using Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective. Compare the two recorded constant-module presentations through their canonical coefficient-ring isomorphism. The finite-free scalar-extension theorem identifies the extension of the constant A^r with the finite power of the regular completed coefficient module. Mapping the splitting yields a retract of this power, including r=0.

proof.text: The regular module of a limit of ring sheaves is the limit of the regular modules of the finite levels, restricted along the cone maps. Prove this by forgetting to module presheaves, evaluating, and forgetting to additive groups; all these functors preserve or reflect the relevant limits. The same calculation after slice restriction follows from its sectionwise preservation of limits. By the canonical quotient-kernel formula, every element in the kernel of the first projection has nilpotent image at every finite level: the kernel is generated by constant elements of I, each of whose (n+1)st powers lies in the kernel at level n, and the nilpotent elements form an ideal.

source.place: Tag 099Q; sites-modules.tex Tags 093J, 093M and 03EL; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YQ and 0E8K; finite-projective model calculation in Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.6.11.

proof.text: For a nilpotent endomorphism, the shift on a countable product is nilpotent, so 1 minus that shift is invertible by a finite geometric series. Apply this to multiplication by a kernel element on each finite quotient. The multiplication-difference natural transformation commutes with limits, so it is invertible on the regular completed module, on finite powers, and on their retracts. Exact countable products on each pro-etale slice and the multiplication-difference criterion give the required local internal-Hom vanishing for the whole complex. For a slice of a slice, transport exact products through Over.iteratedSliceEquiv; restrict the same ring cone and finite-projective splittings. This proves precisely kernel completeness both globally and on every slice, without any ULift coefficient transport or restriction-of-scalars completeness theorem.

proof.text: A projective algebraic module is flat. Exact constant realization and scalar extension preserve site-flatness, and the canonical tensor comparison identifies it with categorical flatness for the actual model. Boundedness above makes the complex K-flat. The universal derived scalar-extension comparison is therefore invertible. Exact restriction preserves K-flatness on every slice.

source.place: Tag 099Q; sites-modules.tex Tags 093J, 093M and 03EL; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YQ and 0E8K; finite-projective model calculation in Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.6.11.

proof.text: Construct scalar-extension composition by uniqueness of left adjoints to the composed restriction functors. The adjunction unit equation fixes its value on 1 tensor (1 tensor m); linearity gives the formula on arbitrary tensor generators. The coefficient map followed by the first projection is the constant quotient map. The normalized constant-realization scalar-extension comparison therefore gives the canonical residue chain isomorphism with exactly the displayed generator formula. Slice sheafification commutes with restriction, including its unit; its comparison identifies scalar extension on the slice with restriction of scalar extension. Composing it with the global residue isomorphism proves the slice generator formula.

source.place: Tag 099Q; sites-modules.tex Tags 093J, 093M and 03EL; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YQ and 0E8K; finite-projective model calculation in Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.6.11.

proof.text: Over the Noetherian quotient ring, the tensor of each finite term with the quotient is finite. Its cycles are finite as a submodule, and its cohomology is finite as a quotient of those cycles. Exact constant realization commutes with short-complex homology. Compose this comparison with the derived localization homology factorization and the invertible derived residue map. Exact slice restriction gives the identical calculation on slices. Outside [a,b], the actual terms vanish; their homology and therefore their derived cohomology vanish. This also covers a>b and the zero complex.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q134-e6ead4840 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The 7-step split creates no new node and keeps the statement and stmt_deps unchanged. It matches the reverse direction of Bhatt–Scholze Prop 6.6.11 (via Lemma 6.5.8 and the residue of the constant model). Step checks: (1) a finite projective P^i is the image of an idempotent e_i, so M^i ≅ lim (P^i/I^n P^i)_T by sectionwise limits and exact constant sheaves. (2) lem-weil-pbc-torsion-limit-sheaf-completeness covers bounded complexes of such limits, and lem-weil-pbc-restriction-local-completeness (an iff with no hypotheses; its JB is the item's IB) gives locally derived IB-complete. (3) The quotient clause of the constant-completion equivalence at n=1 gives B/IB = k. (4) Summands of B^r are flat, the complex is bounded above so it is K-flat, and derived change of rings is computed on K-flat complexes, so no Tor hypothesis is needed. (5) The chain isomorphism holds degreewise through e_i and is natural in d. (6) The constant functor is exact and each term is a summand of k^r, so the cohomology is finite-dimensional and vanishes outside [a,b]. (7) Weakly étale localization, restriction commuting with tensor, and restriction preserving K-flat complexes give the slice case. Stacks tags 093J, 093M, 06YQ, 0E8K, 03EL, 099Q and 099C were checked in the tag table. Edge cases checked: Z_(p); k[e]/e^2 with I=(e); a field with I=0; the zero complex; an infinite residue field. The statement gives exactly what parent lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect uses in its steps 4 and 5. The nine generic module-sheaf tool_uses are accepted. Live and side-live still have the item unsplit. Maintainer note: the item's source.place, and also lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site, cite Tag 06YS for lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; the correct tag is 06YQ. Both are maintainer-owned fields, so I did not fix them.

The canonical global and slice chain isomorphisms are fixed by their local tensor-generator formulas.
